headline: Westlake swings to profit as PEM rebounds, debt falls
summary_short: Westlake posted Q2 2026 net income of $260M ($2.01 diluted EPS) on net sales of $3,271M, a turnaround from a $169M net loss in Q1 2026 and a $142M net loss in Q2 2025, as EBITDA rose to $679M from $150M and $210M respectively.
summary_long: Net sales rose 10.8% y/y to $3,271M as PEM's average price gained 14% y/y on polyethylene/PVC strength and HIP volumes grew on pipe & fittings demand plus the ACI acquisition. Operating income swung to $364M from losses of $172M (Q1) and $109M (Q2 2025), helped by the absence of $85M Identified Items (litigation settlement + facility shutdowns) in Q1 and $130M of shutdown charges a year earlier. PEM EBITDA rebounded to $416M from $19M/$(78)M; HIP EBITDA held near $276M. Westlake redeemed $500M of senior notes, cutting short-term debt to zero, and returned $99M to shareholders via dividends/buybacks. Cash fell to $1,643M from $2,724M at year-end. No new numeric guidance issued.

EBITDA quirk: the release's own '+100% y/y' EBITDA comparison ($679M vs $340M) nets Q2 2026's zero Identified Items against Q2 2025's $130M of Identified Items — i.e. it compares GAAP EBITDA this quarter to a non-GAAP ex-items EBITDA a year ago, not like-for-like GAAP-to-GAAP (GAAP EBITDA was $210M in Q2 2025, which would be +223%). The KPI table uses the company's own headline comparison per ledger discipline, with this basis difference flagged here. EPS: basic ($2.02) and diluted ($2.01) differ slightly; diluted is used in the KPI table per convention. The Q1 2026 → Q2 2026 operating-income swing was aided by the absence of Identified Items: Q1 2026 carried a $67M PVC-pipe-fittings litigation settlement plus $18M of facility-shutdown charges; Q2 2025 carried $130M of shutdown/inventory charges; Q2 2026 had none.

drivers.explanation: CEO cites PEM's leverage to improving supply-demand fundamentals, including Strait of Hormuz-related disruptions, plus last year's footprint optimization and cost actions; CFO cites a return to free cash flow generation and a new $1.5B revolver replacing one expiring 2027.
Higher PEM average selling price (+14% y/y, on polyethylene and PVC resin) and higher HIP/PEM sales volume, plus the January 2026 ACI acquisition, drove the increase.

PEM swung to profit on the 14% price gain and three-pillar plan savings; HIP income dipped y/y on lower pipe & fittings pricing despite volume growth; zero Identified Items this quarter (vs $130M a year ago) also lifted the total.

Company attributes the improvement to PEM price/margin gains and its three-pillar profitability plan, which it says is on track to deliver a cumulative $600M operating-income benefit (no period specified); Q1 2026 and Q2 2025 EBITDA were held down by $85M and $130M of Identified Items respectively, versus none this quarter.

Company redeemed the remaining approximately $500M of its 3.60% 2026 senior notes during the quarter and replaced its revolving credit facility (2027 expiration) with a new $1.5B revolver expiring 2031.
Fell to zero because Westlake redeemed the remaining approximately $500M of outstanding 3.60% 2026 Senior Notes during the quarter, which had been the current portion.
Cash fell $628M q/q; disclosed components account for most of it: the ~$500M senior-note redemption and $99M of dividends/buybacks, partly offset by $318M of quarterly operating cash flow.
